Create the cover illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: A wide view of a sunny country road winding through meadows of buttercups and daisies. On one side of the road, the Tiny Grass Maiden sits upright in a shining silver tablespoon drawn by two little white mice, holding reins of red thread and smiling proudly. On the far side of the road, Askeladden rides his dun horse at a slow, careful walk, leaning out of the saddle to keep an anxious eye on her.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A tall, gangly young prince of about nineteen with long arms and legs, a long face with deep dimples when he smiles, warm hazel eyes, a straight nose and copper-red hair cut in a round bowl cut. He wears a sky-blue linen smock with a small silver clasp at the collar, belted with a broad brown leather belt, loose grey wool breeches and tall, worn brown riding boots.
- the Tiny Grass Maiden: A tiny young woman of about eighteen, no taller than a man's hand, perfectly formed with the natural proportions of a grown girl, slim and light on her feet, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a bright smile. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long plaits tied with grass-green ribbons, with daisies tucked in. She wears a fine ankle-length white linen dress with a grass-green sash, and a faint glow shines about her.

Story world: Old rural Norway in early summer. The King's manor is a large royal farm of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved dragon gables and a wide yard, among flowering meadows. The road from the manor runs through the meadows past the tussock where the Doll in the Grass lives: a round, knee-high hump of grass and clover that parts like a curtain, with a snug little room beneath it. The tiny shirt is snow-white linen, no longer than a man's finger. Her carriage is an ordinary shining silver tablespoon drawn by two little white mice with reins of red thread. Further on, the road runs along a great, wide, dark lake fringed with reeds. Askeladden's horse is a dun fjord horse with a black-and-cream striped mane.

This story's season, light and colours: Early summer: meadows full of buttercups, clover, cornflowers and white daisies, fresh green birches and soft morning light under a pale-blue sky with small white clouds. The great lake is dark slate-blue under drifting cloud. The homecoming is a grey, rain-washed afternoon with puddles and dripping eaves. Accents: shining silver, grass green and sky blue.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. characters.name: The King
characters.description: Father of twelve sons, stern in his demands but quick to recognize true worth when Ash-Lad returns with a remarkable bride.

characters.name: The Merman
characters.description: A mysterious being of the water who returns the Doll in the Grass and triggers her wondrous transformation.

The great lake is dark slate-blue under drifting cloud. The homecoming is a grey, rain-washed afternoon with puddles and dripping eaves. Accents: shining silver, grass green and sky blue.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
